title: Step Base
description: Shared base properties for all pipeline step schemas. Does not set additionalProperties — intended as a composable fragment.

$schema.description: JSON Schema URI identifying the schema this artifact conforms to. Format: vc:{NN}-{step-name}. Examples: 'vc:00-charter' for a charter artifact, 'vc:01-capabilities' for capabilities, 'vc:04-fr-list' for FR list. Must match the $id of the step schema exactly as registered in schema_registry.json. Do NOT use HTTP URLs — the registry uses vc: URNs. An incorrect URI here causes schema resolution to fail silently.

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this artifact instance. Convention: {step-noun}-v{N}. Examples: 'charter-v1', 'capabilities-v1', 'fr-list-v1', 'system-sketch-v1', 'nfrs-v1'. Increment the version suffix only on full regeneration of the artifact. Anti-pattern: using a capability or FR prefix (cap-*, fr-*) for an artifact-level ID — those prefixes are reserved for items within the artifact, not the artifact itself.

owner.description: Owner of this spec artifact. Must be one of 8 canonical values: 'api' (backend services), 'ui' (frontend/UX), 'system' (platform/infrastructure), 'ops' (operations/DevOps), 'data' (data engineering/analytics), 'product' (product management), 'business' (business stakeholders), 'engineering' (general engineering). Choose the team that creates, maintains, and is accountable for this artifact. Authoritative list also maintained in canon/kinds/owner.json.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this artifact was generated or last regenerated. Always use UTC with Z suffix. Example: '2025-10-16T22:06:04.202593Z'. Update this field whenever the artifact is fully regenerated from scratch. Do not update it for minor edits — use a separate updated_at field if tracking incremental changes.

canonical_refs_used.description: Aggregate list of every canonical registry reference used anywhere in this artifact. Aggregation rule: collect one entry per unique `id` from all `*_ref` fields (capability_ref, entity_ref, unit_ref, status_ref, etc.) across the entire document, deduplicated. Example: if you wrote {"id": "cn:project:term:billing-amount", "kind": "term"} in two different fields, include it once here. Required even when empty — use [] when no canonical references were made. Validated by canonical-integrity checks at build time.

canonical_proposals.description: Optional by default; individual step schemas may promote this to required (e.g., 03_glossary). Array of proposed canonical entries discovered during this step's analysis. Decision rule: populate this field whenever the AI generator encounters a domain concept that (a) does not yet exist in the canon registry and (b) appears in a field that accepts a canonical reference (e.g., capability_ref, entity_ref, unit_ref). Omit entirely if no new canonical terms were identified — do not include an empty array unless the step schema requires it. Example: Step 01 introduces a new capability concept 'merchant-account' not in the registry — add a proposal: {"temp_id": "merchant-account", "kind": "entity", "proposed_label": "Merchant Account", "definition": "A business entity registered to accept payments through the platform.", "source_field": "capabilities[*].capability_ref"}. Example: Step 04 introduces a new action verb 'reconcile' not in the registry — add a proposal with kind 'action'. Anti-pattern: adding a proposal for a concept that already exists in the canon registry under a different label — check aliases.json first, as the existing entry may already cover the concept under an alternate name.

canonical_conflicts.description: Optional. Array of conflicts between proposed canonical entries and existing registry entries, produced by canonical-autofix tooling — do not author manually. When present (non-empty), each entry identifies a field_path where an input value matched multiple canon entries and could not be auto-resolved. Omit entirely if no conflicts were detected. Structure per entry: {field_path: string, input_value: string, candidate_ids: [cn:id-1, cn:id-2], reason: string}.

items.description: A migration annotation string added by canonical-autofix or align tooling.

_migration_notes.description: Optional migration annotations added by canonical-autofix or align tooling during schema migrations. Do NOT populate this field manually — it is written exclusively by specdev tooling (canonical-autofix, align apply). Human authors should leave this field absent. If present after a tooling run, it documents what was auto-corrected and should be reviewed before committing.
